extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their accountants/financial reporting teams (preparers, auditors, and legal/SEC reporting personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and explanatory guidance from the SEC final rules on disclosing climate-related effects in consolidated financial statements, including thresholds, required line-item and contextual disclosures for severe weather, other natural conditions, and carbon offsets/RECs, and Rule 14-02(h) disclosures about impacts on financial estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No separate threshold determination for carbon offsets and RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the disclosures related to severe weather events and other natural conditions, a registrant is not required to separately determine whether the disclosure threshold is triggered for costs, expenditures, and losses that are recorded on the balance sheet versus the income statement for disclosures related to carbon offsets and RECs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with severe-weather/natural-condition disclosure approach; for carbon offsets/RECs do not split threshold calculations between balance sheet and income statement presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosure when carbon offsets/RECs are a material component of plans
rubrics_metrics.description: If disclosure is required because carbon offsets or RECs have been used as a material component of a registrant's plan to achieve its disclosed climate-related targets or goals, then a registrant must separately disclose: (1) the aggregate amount of each of the capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and RECs during the fiscal year; (2) the beginning and ending balances of capitalized carbon offsets and RECs on the balance sheet for the fiscal year; and (3) where on the balance sheet and the income statement the capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and RECs are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the three elements for the fiscal year (aggregate flows, opening/closing balances, and presentation location). Example tables in the release illustrate formatting. Registrants should consider facts and circumstances and disclose accounting policy for carbon offsets/RECs (see 17 CFR 210.14-02(e)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of contextual information for financial statement effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Required contextual information may include disclosure such as the specific severe weather events, natural conditions, and transactions that were aggregated for purposes of determining the effects on the balance sheet and income statement amounts and, if applicable, policy decisions made by a registrant, such as any significant judgments made to determine the amount of capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: identify specific events aggregated; disclose policy decisions and significant judgments; disclose insurance recoveries recognized (e.g., $400,000) and where presented on the statements. Contextual disclosure helps users understand nature of business effects and the aggregation approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and disclose where expenditures/costs/charges/losses/recoveries are presented
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require registrants to first identify the relevant expenditures, costs, charges, losses, and recoveries and then separately disclose where on the balance sheet and income statement these costs and expenditures are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to address dispersed presentation across multiple line items and provide consistency and comparability; examples show mapping to balance sheet (asset lines) and income statement (expense or other income/(loss)) line items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate disclosure of expenditures expensed and losses as incurred (examples of covered items)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may be required to disclose the aggregate amount of expenditures expensed and losses as incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions, for example, to restore operations, relocate assets or operations affected by the event or condition, retire affected assets, repair affected assets, recognize impairment loss of affected assets, or otherwise respond to the effect that severe weather events and other natural conditions had on business operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, the final rules may require disclosure of aggregate capitalized costs and charges incurred for similar remediation/repair/replace/impairment activities. The disclosure is line-item focused and tied to the attribution principle for events/conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 14-02(h): Disclosure about material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require registrants to disclose whether the estimates and assumptions used to produce the consolidated financial statements were materially impacted by exposures to risks and uncertainties associated with, or known impacts from, severe weather events and other natural conditions, such as hurricanes, tornadoes, flooding, drought, wildfires, extreme temperatures, and sea level rise, or any climate-related targets or transition plans disclosed by the registrant. If so, registrants must provide a qualitative description of how the development of such estimates and assumptions were impacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of transition activity disclosure was narrowed to only transition plans disclosed by the registrant. The materiality qualifier was added (only materially impacted estimates/assumptions must be disclosed). The required disclosure is qualitative (not necessarily quantitative) and intended to help investors evaluate reasonableness, resilience, and comparative analysis against peers; it will be located in a single note to the financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality qualifier for estimates and assumptions disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require registrants to disclose whether the estimates and assumptions used to prepare the consolidated financial statements were materially impacted by exposures to risks and uncertainties associated with, or known impacts from, severe weather events and other natural conditions, or any climate-related targets or transition plans disclosed by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This focuses management on a narrower set of impacts to reduce operational burden and avoid producing immaterial information. The SEC considered and rejected adding a second materiality qualifier (e.g., ‘material’ estimates that are ‘materially impacted’) as unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of disclosure in a single financial statement note
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure regarding material impacts to estimates and assumptions will be located in a single note to the financial statements along with the other financial statement disclosures adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locating disclosures in a single note enhances usefulness by collocating climate-impact information with the other financial statement disclosures; distinguishes this disclosure from critical accounting estimates that are often presented outside the financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of estimates and assumptions that may require disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statement estimates and assumptions that may require disclosure pursuant to the final rules may include those related to the estimated salvage value of certain assets, estimated useful life of certain assets, projected financial information used in impairment calculations, estimated loss contingencies, estimated reserves (such as environmental reserves, asset retirement obligations, or loan loss allowances), estimated credit risks, fair value measurement of certain assets, and commodity price assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are example categories (not an exhaustive list). Registrants should consider which material estimates and assumptions were materially impacted and provide qualitative disclosure about how they were affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to disclose material changes in estimates/assumptions among fiscal years
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC considered whether to require disclosure of material changes in estimates, assumptions, or methodology among fiscal years and the reasons for those changes, but at this time is not including such a requirement in the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the narrower scope of the final rules (focused on discrete transactions recognized in financial statements under GAAP) reduces need for explicit multi-year change disclosures; current GAAP requirements for material changes remain applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities disclosure not adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC decided not to adopt the proposed rules related to the disclosure of opportunities. The final rules do not make a distinction between 'risks' and 'opportunities' in the financial statement disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the financial impact metrics and other proposed items were not adopted, the SEC removed the separate opportunities disclosure. If a cost or expenditure was incurred as a result of a severe weather event or natural condition in furtherance of an opportunity, the cost/expenditure would still be disclosed (assuming other requirements are met) but registrants are not required to identify costs as related to an 'opportunity.' The SEC noted concerns about forward-looking/speculative nature, auditability, greenwashing, and competitive sensitivity as reasons commenters favored optional treatment originally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose accounting policy for carbon offsets and RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should disclose their accounting policy for carbon offsets and RECs in accordance with 17 CFR 210.14-02(e)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release notes diversity in practice (some entities capitalize costs and present offsets/RECs in intangible assets, others expense them). The example provided is illustrative and not a preferred method; registrants should consider facts and circumstances when determining accounting treatment and disclose the policy accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of insurance recoveries and their presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the contextual information, a registrant would be required to disclose insurance recoveries recognized in the consolidated financial statements as a result of severe weather events, including identification of where the recoveries are presented in the income statement or balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in the release discloses $400,000 in insurance recoveries and specifies presentation; such recoveries should be included when identifying and explaining financial statement effects.
